1nixxxe:246: The most important contribution of this survey is establishing harness engineering as an independent system layer. Traditionally, the reliability of LLM systems was attributed to the capabilities of the model itself—parameter scale, pretraining data quality, and instruction-tuning quality. However, deployment practices since 2025 show that once model capability crosses a certain threshold, task execution reliability increasingly depends on the wrapping infrastructure rather than the model itself. This insight is highly significant for industry: improving system reliability does not have to wait for the next GPT-5-level model release—by optimizing each layer of the harness, significant gains can be achieved.

1vbnnpm:309: The survey highlights a notable industry evolution trend: from agent frameworks to agent platforms. Frameworks focus on local abstractions (agent, tool, memory, execution loop), while platforms add persistent workspaces, identity authentication, observability, evaluation, governance, and human handoff. This shift means LLM agent engineering is maturing—moving from proof of concept to production deployment requires a complete infrastructure stack, not point tools. It also signals the future direction of industry consolidation: vertically integrated agent platforms will be more competitive than fragmented toolchains.
